title: BigP3BCI Study K — 9x8 adaptive/checkerboard, 2 sessions (5 healthy subjects)
description: BigP3BCI Study K is a derivative EEG dataset containing P300 brain-computer interface recordings from 5 healthy subjects across 2 sessions using a 9x8 adaptive/checkerboard visual stimulus paradigm. The dataset comprises 16-channel EEG data sampled at 256 Hz with target and non-target event classifications, designed for P300-based speller applications. This dataset is part of the larger BigP3BCI project, the largest public P300 BCI dataset containing recordings from approximately 267 subjects across 20 studies.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a g.USBamp amplifier (g.tec) with 16 channels arranged in a standard 10-20 montage at a sampling rate of 256 Hz with 60 Hz line frequency filtering. Subjects performed a P300 speller task using a 9x8 character grid with adaptive/checkerboard stimulus presentation. Each session included target and non-target visual stimuli with a trial interval of 0-1.0 seconds. HED 8.4.0 event annotations were applied to classify sensory events as target or non-target visual presentations.
